The button is enabled (`disabled: false`) and visible, so nothing about its own state warns the learner; the click is simply delivered to the nav instead.\n\n**Evidence (reproducible, no pointer events synthesised):**\n\n- `docs/audits/evidence/modal-occlusion/modal-occlusion-report.json` — baseline `main`.\n- `docs/audits/evidence/modal-occlusion-pr15-fix/modal-occlusion-report.json` — PR #15 head, with a collection selected so the button is enabled.\n- Screenshots: `save-sheet-mobile-390x844.png`, `save-sheet-desktop-1365x900.png` in both directories.\n- Harness: `scripts/modal-occlusion-probe.mjs`.\n\n### 2.1 Root cause (Verified by direct manipulation)\n\nThe sheet is a `fixed inset-0` overlay, but it is mounted **inside a FEED card** that carries `backdrop-blur-xl`:\n\n- `src/components/feed/FeedScreen.tsx:153` and `:162` — the feed card: `rounded-[2rem] bg-white/10 backdrop-blur-xl …`\n- `src/components/collections/SaveLikeButton.tsx:89` — renders `<SaveToCollectionModal …>` from inside that card.\n- `src/components/collections/SaveToCollectionModal.tsx:69` — the overlay: `fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-black/60 backdrop-blur-xs …`\n\nPer CSS, an element whose `backdrop-filter` is not `none` becomes the **containing block for its `position: fixed` descendants**. The feed card therefore captures the sheet's `fixed inset-0`, and `inset-0` resolves to the card's box — which is why the recorded sheet rect (397–697) does not match the button position (761–789). The card's own stacking context also traps the `z-50` overlay, so the app's sticky bottom nav (`z-40`, a sibling) paints over the sheet footer.\n\n**Decisive confirmation.** Neutralising the ancestor's backdrop filter — exactly what moving the sheet to a document-level portal would achieve — changed the outcome from failure to success with no other change:\n\n```\nBEFORE: {\"center\":[279,775],\"hit\":\"NAV\",\"isBtn\":false}\nAFTER neutralizing backdrop-filter: {\"hit\":\"SPAN\",\"isBtn\":false}   # sheet re-anchored to the viewport, button moved to 636-664\npointer click with stacking context neutralized: saved_items 0 -> 1\n```\n\nThe same script showed that dispatching the button's own DOM `.click()` also saves (`saved_items 0 -> 1`), which is why a script that bypasses hit-testing (a common Playwright workaround) reports success while a learner's real tap does nothing.\n\n### 2.2 Why PR #15's guard does not resolve it\n\n| Check | Baseline `main` | PR #15 (`ec4f48ef74`) |\n|---|---|---|\n| Save enabled with no collection | Yes (defect F-01) | **No — correctly disabled** |\n| Save enabled with a collection ticked | Yes | Yes |\n| Button centre hit-tests to the button | **No (`NAV`)** | **No (`NAV`)** |\n| Real pointer click saves the item | **No** | **No** (only a synthetic DOM click does) |\n\nPR #15 is a correct and necessary fix for F-01. It is **not sufficient** for the learner-facing flow: after ticking a collection, the button is enabled but still covered, so the sheet appears frozen. This is a second, independent finding rather than a re-report of F-01.\n\n### 2.3 Impact\n\n- The learner taps the enabled \"Save Item\" button and nothing happens; the sheet stays open with no feedback.\n- This affects **both** mobile and desktop, and every FEED card, not just the one exercised here.\n- It also invalidates any browser evidence that used a DOM-dispatched click to prove the save loop works, because that path is not what a learner does. The companion report's task-5 result must be read with this in mind: its FAIL is real, and a PASS obtained by force-clicking would be a false positive.\n\n### 2.4 Smallest safe fix (for a separate PR, not this audit)\n\nRender the sheet at document level so it is not captured by the feed card. The minimal, behaviour-preserving option is to portal it, e.g. mount `SaveToCollectionModal` (and the other `fixed inset-0` sheets) with `createPortal(..., document.body)`, or hoist it out of the blurred card in `FeedScreen`. Keep the visual markup and the `z-50` layer; do not change copy or the save logic. Add a regression test that **hit-tests** the button rather than dispatching a synthetic click, so the class of bug cannot return silently. This is a layout/portal change, so it belongs in its own PR and should be reviewed as a UI change, not folded into the typecheck or audit work.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Status of the other reported items at this checkpoint\n\nRe-checked against the live repository and API at 2026-10-22T11:36Z.\n\n| Item | Status | Evidence |\n|---|---|---|\n| F-01 save-with-no-collection | **Fix proposed** — PR #15 `ec4f48ef74`, guard verified, integrity 69/69 | PR #15; `npm run test:integrity` |\n| F-04 typecheck gate | **Fix proposed twice** — PR #11 `3abfa2e181` and PR #12 `25388f8188`; both CI-green | `npm run lint` on `main` = 11 errors (exit 1), reproduced; both PRs' runs `success` |\n| F-08 sheet occlusion | **Open, verified** — see §2 | occlusion probe JSON + screenshots |\n| F-02 branding, F-03 French copy | **Open, unchanged** | companion report §4 |\n| F-06 deployment identity | **Still Blocked** — no deployed URL; `amina.onrender.com/api/health` → 404; Pages site → 404; Pages API → 404 | live probes; `render.yaml` |\n| R1 audit report | **Delivered** on `audit/amina-forensic-2026-10-22` | `docs/audits/AMINA_FORENSIC_AUDIT_2026-10-22.md` |\n| R3 learner-flow evidence | **Delivered**, 9/10 PASS in the independent rerun; task 5 FAIL is F-08 | companion report §5; this addendum §2 |\n\n**R2 note (Observed-not-verified, needs an owner decision).** `main`'s `tsconfig.json` does **not** set `strict: true`. PR #12 adds `\"strict\": true` and `\"allowUnreachableCode\": false`; PR #11 fixes the same errors without tightening the config. Both make the gate blocking. \"Strict TypeScript gate\" is satisfied more literally by the PR that also turns on `strict`, but the two PRs overlap and one should be chosen and the other closed to avoid divergent fixes to the same files.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Severity-ranked findings\n\n### F-01 — Saved items can be filed into no collection and then appear lost (P1, functional)\n- **Verified.** Learner-flow task 5 FAIL. Sequence: FEED card → \"Save to Collection\" → modal → \"Save Item\". The modal's Save button is only disabled while `isSaving`, so it is clickable with zero collections selected (`SaveToCollectionModal.tsx:196`). `handleSave` then calls `saveContent` with `collectionIds: []`; `saveItem` persists the item, and `handleSaveContent` shows the toast \"Saved to collection\" (`AppContext.tsx:926`).\n- **Exact behaviour (Verified in source + capture):** the item *is* written to storage, so it still appears under Review → Saved Items → \"All Saves\" (`ReviewScreen.tsx:67`, which lists all `savedItems`). But it belongs to no collection, so the **\"Saved & Collections\" screen shows \"Nothing saved here yet.\"** while the success toast is still on screen. Default collections always exist at this point (ensured in `AppContext.tsx:340`), so this is purely \"the learner did not tick a box\", not \"no collections exist\".\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/learner-flow/task5-collections.png` — empty collection list and the \"Saved to collection\" toast in the same capture. `artifacts/learner-flow/learner-flow-report.json` (task 5 detail).\n- **Impact:** the confirmation message and the \"Saved & Collections\" destination both imply the item was filed somewhere it can be reopened; instead it is unfiled and invisible on that screen. It is a trust and findability defect in the save/revisit loop, not total data loss.\n- **Smallest safe fix (for a separate PR, not this audit):** in `SaveToCollectionModal.handleSave`, when `selectedColIds` is empty, either require a selection (disable Save until one is chosen) or default to a real collection before persisting. Either way the toast must reflect reality. Default collections always exist at this point (ensured in `AppContext.tsx:340`), so this is purely \"the learner did not tick a box\", not \"no collections exist\".\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/learner-flow/task5-collections.png` — empty collection list and the \"Saved to collection\" toast in the same capture. `artifacts/learner-flow/learner-flow-report.json` (task 5 detail).\n- **Impact:** the confirmation message and the \"Saved & Collections\" destination both imply the item was filed somewhere it can be reopened; instead it is unfiled and invisible on that screen. It is a trust and findability defect in the save/revisit loop, not total data loss.\n- **Smallest safe fix (for a separate PR, not this audit):** in `SaveToCollectionModal.handleSave`, when `selectedColIds` is empty, either require a selection (disable Save until one is chosen) or default to a real collection before persisting. Either way the toast must reflect reality. Behaviour-preserving elsewhere.\n- **Update 2026-10-22T11:36Z:** a guard for this is now proposed on PR #15 (`ec4f48ef74`) and independently re-checked here (guard present, integrity 69/69). **But the guard alone does not make the flow work** — see **F-08** in `AMINA_AUDIT_ADDENDUM_MODAL_OCCLUSION_2026-10-22.md`: the same button is physically covered by the bottom nav, so even an enabled button does nothing on a real tap. Harness check \"product brand and teacher identity are distinct\" expects both \"Amina\" and \"Miss Nour\" and FAILs on `main`.\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/design-audit/04-home-mobile.png`; harness check list in `artifacts/design-audit/report.json`.\n- **Note:** the design branch (PR #7) reports a fix (\"header title is now 'Amina'\"). Severity-ranked findings\n\n### F-01 — Saved items can be filed into no collection and then appear lost (P1, functional)\n- **Verified.** Learner-flow task 5 FAIL. Sequence: FEED card → \"Save to Collection\" → modal → \"Save Item\". The modal's Save button is only disabled while `isSaving`, so it is clickable with zero collections selected (`SaveToCollectionModal.tsx:196`). `handleSave` then calls `saveContent` with `collectionIds: []`; `saveItem` persists the item, and `handleSaveContent` shows the toast \"Saved to collection\" (`AppContext.tsx:926`).\n- **Exact behaviour (Verified in source + capture):** the item *is* written to storage, so it still appears under Review → Saved Items → \"All Saves\" (`ReviewScreen.tsx:67`, which lists all `savedItems`). But it belongs to no collection, so the **\"Saved & Collections\" screen shows \"Nothing saved here yet.\"** while the success toast is still on screen. Default collections always exist at this point (ensured in `AppContext.tsx:340`), so this is purely \"the learner did not tick a box\", not \"no collections exist\".\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/learner-flow/task5-collections.png` — empty collection list and the \"Saved to collection\" toast in the same capture. `artifacts/learner-flow/learner-flow-report.json` (task 5 detail).\n- **Impact:** the confirmation message and the \"Saved & Collections\" destination both imply the item was filed somewhere it can be reopened; instead it is unfiled and invisible on that screen. It is a trust and findability defect in the save/revisit loop, not total data loss.\n- **Smallest safe fix (for a separate PR, not this audit):** in `SaveToCollectionModal.handleSave`, when `selectedColIds` is empty, either require a selection (disable Save until one is chosen) or default to a real collection before persisting. Either way the toast must reflect reality. Behaviour-preserving elsewhere.\n- **Update 2026-10-22T11:36Z:** a guard for this is now proposed on PR #15 (`ec4f48ef74`) and independently re-checked here (guard present, integrity 69/69). **But the guard alone does not make the flow work** — see **F-08** in `AMINA_AUDIT_ADDENDUM_MODAL_OCCLUSION_2026-10-22.md`: the same button is physically covered by the bottom nav, so even an enabled button does nothing on a real tap. F-01 and F-08 must both be fixed for the save/revisit loop to work.\n\n### F-02 — Product identity and teacher identity are conflated (P2, branding)\n- **Verified** on `main`. The persistent header renders \"Miss Nour\" as the app title with the learner name beneath (`AppShell.tsx`). Harness check \"product brand and teacher identity are distinct\" expects both \"Amina\" and \"Miss Nour\" and FAILs on `main`.\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/design-audit/04-home-mobile.png`; harness check list in `artifacts/design-audit/report.json`.\n- **Note:** the design branch (PR #7) reports a fix (\"header title is now 'Amina'\"). That fix is **PR-only**, not on `main`.\n\n### F-03 — French selection yields mixed-language UI (P1, localization)\n- **Verified** on `main`. With French selected: HOME shows \"Welcome, Learner QA!\", \"Your personal AI School Companion\", \"What Should I Do Now, Miss Nour?\"; FEED's intro is English (\"Nour is teaching you now\"); LIBRARY's search placeholder is not French.\n- **Root cause (Observed-not-verified):** `FeedScreen.tsx` only branches on `isAr` for its copy (no `isFr`), and `HomeScreen.tsx:151` has only Arabic/English for the next-action heading. The `fr` dictionary exists in `translations.ts` but those strings are hard-coded.\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/learner-flow/task1-home.png`, `artifacts/design-audit/04-feed-mobile.png`, harness FAIL checks.\n\n### F-04 — The TypeScript quality gate does not block (P1, CI integrity)\n- **Verified, both by reproduction and by CI records.** `npm run lint` on `main` exits 1 with 11 errors, yet CI run [38888767348](https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Amina/actions/runs/38888767348) shows the \"Type check\" step conclusion = **success**. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` sets `continue-on-error: true` on that step.\n- **The 11 errors (Verified):** 8 × TS18047 in `teacherContextEngine.ts` (unreachable code after an unconditional `return` disables narrowing), 2 × TS18047 in `VirtualTeacherClassroom.tsx` (`targetLesson` nullable), 1 × TS2322 in `missionCompletion.ts` (`'practice'` missing from `EvidenceModality`).\n- **Status of the fix:** PR #11 removes `continue-on-error`, deletes the 87-line unreachable block, adds `'practice'` to `EvidenceModality` with an explicit `1.0` weight, and adds optional chaining. Independently verified here: 0 type errors, adaptive 39/39, integrity 72/72, build pass. Follow-up hardening on PR #11 also declares `strict: true` + `allowUnreachableCode: false` explicitly and adds a `strictTypecheckGate` regression suite. I also reproduced the gate failing correctly: a deliberately seeded error made CI run 39770574935 exit 1, proving the step is now blocking. PR #11 is unmerged (draft).\n\n### F-05 — No full digital book reader (P2, product scope)\n- **Observed-not-verified.** `main` has no `BookReader`; \"Open Book\" opens `LessonStudyModal`. The product source of truth (PR #10) asks for full digital books, not only sample cards. Recovery notes indicate `BookReader.tsx` exists on the archive/design branches — so this is a **PR-only** capability, not on `main`.\n\n### F-06 — Production/deployment identity: Pages deployment is stale, Render identity unverified (P1, blocked/partial)\n- **Verified (stronger than a bare probe).** GitHub records exactly one deployment for this repo: deployment `7116513688`, environment `github-pages`, `ref: main`, deployed SHA `a0eda3542170fd3356559b446eb0bcac75790568`, status `success` at 2026-10-16T10:18:06Z, produced by run [38886228008](https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Amina/actions/runs/38886228008).\n- **Verified: that SHA is stale.** GitHub's compare API reports `a0eda354` is **17 commits behind** `main` (`86c1e73`), `ahead_by: 0`. So even the only recorded deployment does not correspond to current `main`.\n- **Verified: the Pages URL is not live.** `GET https://madnessgate44-debug.github.io/Amina/` returns **HTTP 404** with the GitHub Pages \"Site not found\" page, despite the recorded success status. The `deploy-pages.yml` workflow is manual-only (`workflow_dispatch`) and its own header says Pages cannot serve the AI routes (they need `server.ts`).\n- **Blocked: the Render target.** `render.yaml` configures a Render web service named `amina` on branch `main` with health check `/api/health`, but no Render API token or deployed hostname exists in this environment. Probes of `amina.onrender.com`, `amina-1.onrender.com`, and `miss-noor.onrender.com` all returned **404** on `/api/health`, and no `onrender.com` URL is referenced anywhere in the repository.\n- **Conclusion:** the deployed URL/service and deployed SHA are **not verified** for the live app. The one recorded deployment (`a0eda354`) is 17 commits behind `main` and its URL is 404. I did not guess and did not deploy. Closing this needs either the real Render URL + Render account access, or the owner confirming GitHub Pages is not the intended production surface.\n\n### F-07 — AI routes unexercised in this environment (informational)\n- No `GEMINI_API_KEY` was present, so `/api/chat`, `/api/tutor-*`, `/api/stt`, `/api/tts`, `/api/check-homework`, `/api/reconstruct-day` returned their documented degraded fallbacks. The app renders and the degraded paths are honest (\"I can't check this right now…\"), which is correct behaviour — but real model output was **not** exercised here and is **Unverified**.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Default collections always exist at this point (ensured in `AppContext.tsx:340`), so this is purely \"the learner did not tick a box\", not \"no collections exist\".\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/learner-flow/task5-collections.png` — empty collection list and the \"Saved to collection\" toast in the same capture. `artifacts/learner-flow/learner-flow-report.json` (task 5 detail).\n- **Impact:** the confirmation message and the \"Saved & Collections\" destination both imply the item was filed somewhere it can be reopened; instead it is unfiled and invisible on that screen. It is a trust and findability defect in the save/revisit loop, not total data loss.\n- **Smallest safe fix (for a separate PR, not this audit):** in `SaveToCollectionModal.handleSave`, when `selectedColIds` is empty, either require a selection (disable Save until one is chosen) or default to a real collection before persisting. Either way the toast must reflect reality. Behaviour-preserving elsewhere.\n- **Update 2026-10-22T11:36Z:** a guard for this is now proposed on PR #15 (`ec4f48ef74`) and independently re-checked here (guard present, integrity 69/69). **But the guard alone does not make the flow work** — see **F-08** in `AMINA_AUDIT_ADDENDUM_MODAL_OCCLUSION_2026-10-22.md`: the same button is physically covered by the bottom nav, so even an enabled button does nothing on a real tap. F-01 and F-08 must both be fixed for the save/revisit loop to work.\n\n### F-02 — Product identity and teacher identity are conflated (P2, branding)\n- **Verified** on `main`. The persistent header renders \"Miss Nour\" as the app title with the learner name beneath (`AppShell.tsx`). Harness check \"product brand and teacher identity are distinct\" expects both \"Amina\" and \"Miss Nour\" and FAILs on `main`.\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/design-audit/04-home-mobile.png`; harness check list in `artifacts/design-audit/report.json`.\n- **Note:** the design branch (PR #7) reports a fix (\"header title is now 'Amina'\"). That fix is **PR-only**, not on `main`.\n\n### F-03 — French selection yields mixed-language UI (P1, localization)\n- **Verified** on `main`. With French selected: HOME shows \"Welcome, Learner QA!\", \"Your personal AI School Companion\", \"What Should I Do Now, Miss Nour?\"; FEED's intro is English (\"Nour is teaching you now\"); LIBRARY's search placeholder is not French.\n- **Root cause (Observed-not-verified):** `FeedScreen.tsx` only branches on `isAr` for its copy (no `isFr`), and `HomeScreen.tsx:151` has only Arabic/English for the next-action heading. The `fr` dictionary exists in `translations.ts` but those strings are hard-coded.\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/learner-flow/task1-home.png`, `artifacts/design-audit/04-feed-mobile.png`, harness FAIL checks.\n\n### F-04 — The TypeScript quality gate does not block (P1, CI integrity)\n- **Verified, both by reproduction and by CI records.** `npm run lint` on `main` exits 1 with 11 errors, yet CI run [38888767348](https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Amina/actions/runs/38888767348) shows the \"Type check\" step conclusion = **success**. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` sets `continue-on-error: true` on that step.\n- **The 11 errors (Verified):** 8 × TS18047 in `teacherContextEngine.ts` (unreachable code after an unconditional `return` disables narrowing), 2 × TS18047 in `VirtualTeacherClassroom.tsx` (`targetLesson` nullable), 1 × TS2322 in `missionCompletion.ts` (`'practice'` missing from `EvidenceModality`).\n- **Status of the fix:** PR #11 removes `continue-on-error`, deletes the 87-line unreachable block, adds `'practice'` to `EvidenceModality` with an explicit `1.0` weight, and adds optional chaining. Independently verified here: 0 type errors, adaptive 39/39, integrity 72/72, build pass. Follow-up hardening on PR #11 also declares `strict: true` + `allowUnreachableCode: false` explicitly and adds a `strictTypecheckGate` regression suite. I also reproduced the gate failing correctly: a deliberately seeded error made CI run 39770574935 exit 1, proving the step is now blocking. PR #11 is unmerged (draft).\n\n### F-05 — No full digital book reader (P2, product scope)\n- **Observed-not-verified.** `main` has no `BookReader`; \"Open Book\" opens `LessonStudyModal`. The product source of truth (PR #10) asks for full digital books, not only sample cards. Recovery notes indicate `BookReader.tsx` exists on the archive/design branches — so this is a **PR-only** capability, not on `main`.\n\n### F-06 — Production/deployment identity: Pages deployment is stale, Render identity unverified (P1, blocked/partial)\n- **Verified (stronger than a bare probe).** GitHub records exactly one deployment for this repo: deployment `7116513688`, environment `github-pages`, `ref: main`, deployed SHA `a0eda3542170fd3356559b446eb0bcac75790568`, status `success` at 2026-10-16T10:18:06Z, produced by run [38886228008](https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Amina/actions/runs/38886228008).\n- **Verified: that SHA is stale.** GitHub's compare API reports `a0eda354` is **17 commits behind** `main` (`86c1e73`), `ahead_by: 0`. So even the only recorded deployment does not correspond to current `main`.\n- **Verified: the Pages URL is not live.** `GET https://madnessgate44-debug.github.io/Amina/` returns **HTTP 404** with the GitHub Pages \"Site not found\" page, despite the recorded success status. The `deploy-pages.yml` workflow is manual-only (`workflow_dispatch`) and its own header says Pages cannot serve the AI routes (they need `server.ts`).\n- **Blocked: the Render target.** `render.yaml` configures a Render web service named `amina` on branch `main` with health check `/api/health`, but no Render API token or deployed hostname exists in this environment. Probes of `amina.onrender.com`, `amina-1.onrender.com`, and `miss-noor.onrender.com` all returned **404** on `/api/health`, and no `onrender.com` URL is referenced anywhere in the repository.\n- **Conclusion:** the deployed URL/service and deployed SHA are **not verified** for the live app. The one recorded deployment (`a0eda354`) is 17 commits behind `main` and its URL is 404. I did not guess and did not deploy. Closing this needs either the real Render URL + Render account access, or the owner confirming GitHub Pages is not the intended production surface.\n\n### F-07 — AI routes unexercised in this environment (informational)\n- No `GEMINI_API_KEY` was present, so `/api/chat`, `/api/tutor-*`, `/api/stt`, `/api/tts`, `/api/check-homework`, `/api/reconstruct-day` returned their documented degraded fallbacks. Sequence: FEED card → \"Save to Collection\" → modal → \"Save Item\". The modal's Save button is only disabled while `isSaving`, so it is clickable with zero collections selected (`SaveToCollectionModal.tsx:196`). `handleSave` then calls `saveContent` with `collectionIds: []`; `saveItem` persists the item, and `handleSaveContent` shows the toast \"Saved to collection\" (`AppContext.tsx:926`).\n- **Exact behaviour (Verified in source + capture):** the item *is* written to storage, so it still appears under Review → Saved Items → \"All Saves\" (`ReviewScreen.tsx:67`, which lists all `savedItems`). But it belongs to no collection, so the **\"Saved & Collections\" screen shows \"Nothing saved here yet.\"** while the success toast is still on screen. Default collections always exist at this point (ensured in `AppContext.tsx:340`), so this is purely \"the learner did not tick a box\", not \"no collections exist\".\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/learner-flow/task5-collections.png` — empty collection list and the \"Saved to collection\" toast in the same capture. `artifacts/learner-flow/learner-flow-report.json` (task 5 detail).\n- **Impact:** the confirmation message and the \"Saved & Collections\" destination both imply the item was filed somewhere it can be reopened; instead it is unfiled and invisible on that screen. It is a trust and findability defect in the save/revisit loop, not total data loss.\n- **Smallest safe fix (for a separate PR, not this audit):** in `SaveToCollectionModal.handleSave`, when `selectedColIds` is empty, either require a selection (disable Save until one is chosen) or default to a real collection before persisting. Either way the toast must reflect reality. Behaviour-preserving elsewhere.\n- **Update 2026-10-22T11:36Z:** a guard for this is now proposed on PR #15 (`ec4f48ef74`) and independently re-checked here (guard present, integrity 69/69). **But the guard alone does not make the flow work** — see **F-08** in `AMINA_AUDIT_ADDENDUM_MODAL_OCCLUSION_2026-10-22.md`: the same button is physically covered by the bottom nav, so even an enabled button does nothing on a real tap. The `fr` dictionary exists in `translations.ts` but those strings are hard-coded.\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/learner-flow/task1-home.png`, `artifacts/design-audit/04-feed-mobile.png`, harness FAIL checks.\n\n### F-04 — The TypeScript quality gate does not block (P1, CI integrity)\n- **Verified, both by reproduction and by CI records.** `npm run lint` on `main` exits 1 with 11 errors, yet CI run [38888767348](https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Amina/actions/runs/38888767348) shows the \"Type check\" step conclusion = **success**. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` sets `continue-on-error: true` on that step.\n- **The 11 errors (Verified):** 8 × TS18047 in `teacherContextEngine.ts` (unreachable code after an unconditional `return` disables narrowing), 2 × TS18047 in `VirtualTeacherClassroom.tsx` (`targetLesson` nullable), 1 × TS2322 in `missionCompletion.ts` (`'practice'` missing from `EvidenceModality`).\n- **Status of the fix:** PR #11 removes `continue-on-error`, deletes the 87-line unreachable block, adds `'practice'` to `EvidenceModality` with an explicit `1.0` weight, and adds optional chaining. Independently verified here: 0 type errors, adaptive 39/39, integrity 72/72, build pass. Follow-up hardening on PR #11 also declares `strict: true` + `allowUnreachableCode: false` explicitly and adds a `strictTypecheckGate` regression suite. I also reproduced the gate failing correctly: a deliberately seeded error made CI run 39770574935 exit 1, proving the step is now blocking. PR #11 is unmerged (draft).\n\n### F-05 — No full digital book reader (P2, product scope)\n- **Observed-not-verified.** `main` has no `BookReader`; \"Open Book\" opens `LessonStudyModal`. The product source of truth (PR #10) asks for full digital books, not only sample cards. Recovery notes indicate `BookReader.tsx` exists on the archive/design branches — so this is a **PR-only** capability, not on `main`.\n\n### F-06 — Production/deployment identity: Pages deployment is stale, Render identity unverified (P1, blocked/partial)\n- **Verified (stronger than a bare probe).** GitHub records exactly one deployment for this repo: deployment `7116513688`, environment `github-pages`, `ref: main`, deployed SHA `a0eda3542170fd3356559b446eb0bcac75790568`, status `success` at 2026-10-16T10:18:06Z, produced by run [38886228008](https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Amina/actions/runs/38886228008).\n- **Verified: that SHA is stale.** GitHub's compare API reports `a0eda354` is **17 commits behind** `main` (`86c1e73`), `ahead_by: 0`. So even the only recorded deployment does not correspond to current `main`.\n- **Verified: the Pages URL is not live.** `GET https://madnessgate44-debug.github.io/Amina/` returns **HTTP 404** with the GitHub Pages \"Site not found\" page, despite the recorded success status. The `deploy-pages.yml` workflow is manual-only (`workflow_dispatch`) and its own header says Pages cannot serve the AI routes (they need `server.ts`).\n- **Blocked: the Render target.** `render.yaml` configures a Render web service named `amina` on branch `main` with health check `/api/health`, but no Render API token or deployed hostname exists in this environment. Probes of `amina.onrender.com`, `amina-1.onrender.com`, and `miss-noor.onrender.com` all returned **404** on `/api/health`, and no `onrender.com` URL is referenced anywhere in the repository.\n- **Conclusion:** the deployed URL/service and deployed SHA are **not verified** for the live app. The one recorded deployment (`a0eda354`) is 17 commits behind `main` and its URL is 404. I did not guess and did not deploy. Closing this needs either the real Render URL + Render account access, or the owner confirming GitHub Pages is not the intended production surface.\n\n### F-07 — AI routes unexercised in this environment (informational)\n- No `GEMINI_API_KEY` was present, so `/api/chat`, `/api/tutor-*`, `/api/stt`, `/api/tts`, `/api/check-homework`, `/api/reconstruct-day` returned their documented degraded fallbacks. The app renders and the degraded paths are honest (\"I can't check this right now…\"), which is correct behaviour — but real model output was **not** exercised here and is **Unverified**.\n\n### F-08 — The Save-to-Collection confirm button is physically unclickable (P1, functional)\n\n**Verified.** See the companion addendum `AMINA_AUDIT_ADDENDUM_MODAL_OCCLUSION_2026-10-22.md` for the full analysis. In short: the sheet is a `fixed inset-0` overlay mounted inside a FEED card that carries `backdrop-blur-xl`, so the card becomes the containing block for the fixed sheet and its footer lands under the sticky bottom nav. At 390×844 the button's centre hit-tests to `NAV`; at 1365×900 it hits a sibling `SPAN`. A real tap therefore does nothing even though the button is enabled.\n\n- **Independent of F-01, and not fixed by PR #15.** With a collection selected the guard enables the button, but it is still occluded.\n- **Evidence:** `docs/audits/evidence/modal-occlusion/` (baseline) and `docs/audits/evidence/modal-occlusion-pr15-fix/` (PR #15), plus `scripts/modal-occlusion-probe.mjs`.\n- **Impact:** any browser evidence that force-clicks or dispatches a synthetic DOM click in this flow can report a false PASS.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Save an item and find it again | **FAIL** | `task5-save-modal.png`, `task5-collections.png` — two independent causes: F-01 (save allowed with no collection) and F-08 (the confirm button is occluded, so a real tap never fires) |\n| 6. Tasks 4/6 were initially BLOCKED on a harness limitation (modals intercepting nav clicks) and PASS after the harness was corrected — the corrected run is the one reported. The modal's Save button is only disabled while `isSaving`, so it is clickable with zero collections selected (`SaveToCollectionModal.tsx:196`). `handleSave` then calls `saveContent` with `collectionIds: []`; `saveItem` persists the item, and `handleSaveContent` shows the toast \"Saved to collection\" (`AppContext.tsx:926`).\n- **Exact behaviour (Verified in source + capture):** the item *is* written to storage, so it still appears under Review → Saved Items → \"All Saves\" (`ReviewScreen.tsx:67`, which lists all `savedItems`). Default collections always exist at this point (ensured in `AppContext.tsx:340`), so this is purely \"the learner did not tick a box\", not \"no collections exist\".\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/learner-flow/task5-collections.png` — empty collection list and the \"Saved to collection\" toast in the same capture. `artifacts/learner-flow/learner-flow-report.json` (task 5 detail).\n- **Impact:** the confirmation message and the \"Saved & Collections\" destination both imply the item was filed somewhere it can be reopened; instead it is unfiled and invisible on that screen. Either way the toast must reflect reality. With French selected: HOME shows \"Welcome, Learner QA!\", \"Your personal AI School Companion\", \"What Should I Do Now, Miss Nour?\"; FEED's intro is English (\"Nour is teaching you now\"); LIBRARY's search placeholder is not French.\n- **Root cause (Observed-not-verified):** `FeedScreen.tsx` only branches on `isAr` for its copy (no `isFr`), and `HomeScreen.tsx:151` has only Arabic/English for the next-action heading. The `fr` dictionary exists in `translations.ts` but those strings are hard-coded.\n- **Evidence:** `artifacts/learner-flow/task1-home.png`, `artifacts/design-audit/04-feed-mobile.png`, harness FAIL checks.\n\n### F-04 — The TypeScript quality gate does not block (P1, CI integrity)\n- **Verified, both by reproduction and by CI records.** `npm run lint` on `main` exits 1 with 11 errors, yet CI run [38888767348](https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Amina/actions/runs/38888767348) shows the \"Type check\" step conclusion = **success**. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` sets `continue-on-error: true` on that step.\n- **The 11 errors (Verified):** 8 × TS18047 in `teacherContextEngine.ts` (unreachable code after an unconditional `return` disables narrowing), 2 × TS18047 in `VirtualTeacherClassroom.tsx` (`targetLesson` nullable), 1 × TS2322 in `missionCompletion.ts` (`'practice'` missing from `EvidenceModality`).\n- **Status of the fix:** PR #11 removes `continue-on-error`, deletes the 87-line unreachable block, adds `'practice'` to `EvidenceModality` with an explicit `1.0` weight, and adds optional chaining. Independently verified here: 0 type errors, adaptive 39/39, integrity 72/72, build pass. Follow-up hardening on PR #11 also declares `strict: true` + `allowUnreachableCode: false` explicitly and adds a `strictTypecheckGate` regression suite. I also reproduced the gate failing correctly: a deliberately seeded error made CI run 39770574935 exit 1, proving the step is now blocking. PR #11 is unmerged (draft).\n\n### F-05 — No full digital book reader (P2, product scope)\n- **Observed-not-verified.** `main` has no `BookReader`; \"Open Book\" opens `LessonStudyModal`. The product source of truth (PR #10) asks for full digital books, not only sample cards. Recovery notes indicate `BookReader.tsx` exists on the archive/design branches — so this is a **PR-only** capability, not on `main`.\n\n### F-06 — Production/deployment identity: Pages deployment is stale, Render identity unverified (P1, blocked/partial)\n- **Verified (stronger than a bare probe).** GitHub records exactly one deployment for this repo: deployment `7116513688`, environment `github-pages`, `ref: main`, deployed SHA `a0eda3542170fd3356559b446eb0bcac75790568`, status `success` at 2026-10-16T10:18:06Z, produced by run [38886228008](https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Amina/actions/runs/38886228008).\n- **Verified: that SHA is stale.** GitHub's compare API reports `a0eda354` is **17 commits behind** `main` (`86c1e73`), `ahead_by: 0`. So even the only recorded deployment does not correspond to current `main`.\n- **Verified: the Pages URL is not live.** `GET https://madnessgate44-debug.github.io/Amina/` returns **HTTP 404** with the GitHub Pages \"Site not found\" page, despite the recorded success status. The `deploy-pages.yml` workflow is manual-only (`workflow_dispatch`) and its own header says Pages cannot serve the AI routes (they need `server.ts`).\n- **Blocked: the Render target.** `render.yaml` configures a Render web service named `amina` on branch `main` with health check `/api/health`, but no Render API token or deployed hostname exists in this environment. Probes of `amina.onrender.com`, `amina-1.onrender.com`, and `miss-noor.onrender.com` all returned **404** on `/api/health`, and no `onrender.com` URL is referenced anywhere in the repository.\n- **Conclusion:** the deployed URL/service and deployed SHA are **not verified** for the live app. The one recorded deployment (`a0eda354`) is 17 commits behind `main` and its URL is 404. I did not guess and did not deploy. Closing this needs either the real Render URL + Render account access, or the owner confirming GitHub Pages is not the intended production surface.\n\n### F-07 — AI routes unexercised in this environment (informational)\n- No `GEMINI_API_KEY` was present, so `/api/chat`, `/api/tutor-*`, `/api/stt`, `/api/tts`, `/api/check-homework`, `/api/reconstruct-day` returned their documented degraded fallbacks. The app renders and the degraded paths are honest (\"I can't check this right now…\"), which is correct behaviour — but real model output was **not** exercised here and is **Unverified**.\n\n### F-08 — The Save-to-Collection confirm button is physically unclickable (P1, functional)\n\n**Verified.** See the companion addendum `AMINA_AUDIT_ADDENDUM_MODAL_OCCLUSION_2026-10-22.md` for the full analysis. At 390×844 the button's centre hit-tests to `NAV`; at 1365×900 it hits a sibling `SPAN`. A real tap therefore does nothing even though the button is enabled.\n\n- **Independent of F-01, and not fixed by PR #15.** With a collection selected the guard enables the button, but it is still occluded.\n- **Evidence:** `docs/audits/evidence/modal-occlusion/` (baseline) and `docs/audits/evidence/modal-occlusion-pr15-fix/` (PR #15), plus `scripts/modal-occlusion-probe.mjs`.\n- **Impact:** any browser evidence that force-clicks or dispatches a synthetic DOM click in this flow can report a false PASS.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Navigate away from and resume a teaching session | PASS | `task6-nour-open.png`, `task6-nour-resumed.png` |\n| 7. Handle an empty/loading/error state without guessing | PASS | `task7-home-state.png` — empty state explicitly labelled |\n\nCoverage: mobile 390×844 and desktop 1365×900; English onboarding and French learner profile; Arabic RTL verified by the companion audit (`artifacts/design-audit/08-home-arabic-rtl-mobile.png`).\n\n**Explicit limitation:** the walkthrough is a scripted browser run with a synthetic profile. Tasks 4/6 were initially BLOCKED on a harness limitation (modals intercepting nav clicks) and PASS after the harness was corrected — the corrected run is the one reported. A real learner has not been involved; no real child or student data was used.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Confirmed: a normal Playwright click SUCCEEDS on main in both states and both viewports. So my F-08 claim as written ("the button is physically unclickable / a real tap does nothing") is WRONG and overstated. Playwright's click succeeded because it scrolls the element into view first, which moves the nav away.

So what actually happened in my original dbg-t5f? There I clicked after `addStyleTag`... no. In the very first dbg-t5c, the harness used `click({force:true})` and the modal did not close. Hmm, but in dbg-click now, normal click worked. The difference: earlier the harness's T5 used force:true clicks and other state. Also earlier my `dbg-t5f` "pointer click with stacking context neutralized" saved — but I never tested a plain pointer click WITHOUT neutralization in that same script. In dbg-t5c the element at center was NAV, and I concluded occlusion.

So the correct, verified conclusion is:
- The sheet IS misplaced (its footer renders below its own container's bottom edge, into the nav band) — that's a real layout defect (verified geometry: sheet 397–697, button 761–789; overlap with nav 15px/54% on mobile, 3px/11% on desktop).
- A pointer click at the button's centre hits the nav on mobile (verified elementFromPoint). BUT Playwright's high-level click scrolls the element into view first and succeeds.
- Therefore: the button is partially overlapped (bottom ~54% on mobile, ~11% on desktop), and a tap aimed at the overlapped centre region on mobile would be swallowed by the nav — but I have NOT proven that a real user tap fails, because a human taps where the button appears, and the button's top half is clear.

This is a much weaker and more honest finding. I must correct it. The F-08 claim as published on PR #13 and in the issue comment is overstated and I need to retract/correct it immediately.

This is exactly the kind of thing I must not get wrong. Let me correct both the PR description, the addendum doc, and post a correction comment on the issue.

Let me determine the precise truth once more with a decisive test: does a *real touch tap* at the button's visual centre fail? Use touchscreen.tap at the centre coordinate (bypassing auto-scroll). And also test a tap at the top portion.

Let me run that.

So the sheet's `fixed inset-0` is not resolving against the viewport, and the nav paints over the bottom of the button.\n\n### 2.2 What actually happens on a real interaction (the part that matters)\n\nA real pointer click was then sent to specific pixels (raw `mouse.click`, no auto-scroll, no actionability retry):\n\n| Viewport | Raw click at button **centre** | Raw click at button **upper third** |\n|---|---|---|\n| 390×844 mobile | **SWALLOWED** — `saved_items` 0 → 0 | FIRED — `saved_items` 0 → 1 |\n| 1365×900 desktop | FIRED — `saved_items` 0 → 1 | FIRED — `saved_items` 0 → 1 |\n\nAnd a normal Playwright click (which clicks the element's centre with actionability checks) **succeeded on both viewports**: `saved_items 0 → 1`.\n\n**Conclusion, stated precisely:**\n\n- The defect is **real but narrower than first reported**. On mobile, a pointer landing in the bottom ~half of the button is delivered to the nav and does nothing, silently, with no feedback. On desktop the overlap is only 3 px and did not block any tested click.\n- The flow is **not** universally broken, and the earlier \"unclickable at all viewports / F-01's guard is not sufficient\" characterisation was **wrong** and is withdrawn. A learner who taps the button's upper half, or whose browser scrolls it clear, saves successfully.\n\n### 2.3 Root cause (Verified by direct manipulation)\n\nThe sheet is a `fixed inset-0` overlay, but it is mounted **inside a FEED card** that carries `backdrop-blur-xl`:\n\n- `src/components/feed/FeedScreen.tsx:153` and `:162` — the feed card: `rounded-[2rem] bg-white/10 backdrop-blur-xl …`\n- `src/components/collections/SaveLikeButton.tsx:89` — renders `<SaveToCollectionModal …>` from inside that card.\n- `src/components/collections/SaveToCollectionModal.tsx:69` — the overlay: `fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-black/60 backdrop-blur-xs …`\n\nPer CSS, an element whose `backdrop-filter` is not `none` becomes the **containing block for its `position: fixed` descendants** and forms its own stacking context. The feed card therefore captures the sheet's `fixed inset-0`, which is why the recorded sheet rect (397–697) does not match the button position (761–789), and why the card's `z-50` cannot beat the sibling nav's `z-40`.\n\nNeutralising the ancestor's backdrop filter — what a document-level portal achieves — re-anchored the sheet to the viewport and moved the button from `761–789` to `636–664`, clear of the nav at `774`:\n\n```\nBEFORE:                              {\"center\":[279,775],\"hit\":\"NAV\"}\nAFTER neutralizing backdrop-filter:  {\"center\":[301,650],\"hit\":\"SPAN\"}   # button now at 636-664, no overlap\n```\n\n### 2.4 Methodological note: why the first claim was wrong\n\n`document.elementFromPoint(cx, cy)` reports the **topmost element at that pixel**. It is a good occlusion *signal* but it is not proof that a click fails, because it ignores the ancestor chain: a real event is dispatched to the hit target and then **bubbles up through ancestors**, and it only fails if that chain never reaches a handler. Reading \"hit is `NAV`, not the button\" as \"the button is unclickable\" skipped that check.\n\nThe corrected method, used in §2.2, is to send a real pointer event at the coordinates and assert a **side effect** (the IndexedDB `saved_items` count). Practical rules for this repo:\n\n- Never conclude \"broken\" from `elementFromPoint` alone; confirm with a real click and a side-effect assertion.\n- Never conclude \"works\" from `click({force:true})` or an in-page `el.click()` either — both bypass hit-testing and will report a false PASS on a genuinely covered control. Both were used during this investigation; both were misleading here, in opposite directions.\n- Note that a normal Playwright click auto-scrolls the element into view first, so it can succeed on a control a real user cannot currently reach.\n\n### 2.5 Impact and smallest safe fix\n\n**Impact:** low-to-moderate. On a 390 px-wide phone the lower half of the confirm button is dead, so a tap there gives no feedback at all and the learner may believe the save failed. It does not lose data and it does not break the flow for every learner.\n\n**Smallest safe fix (for a separate PR, not this audit):** render the sheet at document level so the feed card does not capture it — `createPortal(..., document.body)` for `SaveToCollectionModal`, or hoist it out of the blurred card in `FeedScreen`. Keep the markup and the `z-50` layer; do not change copy or save logic. This is a layout/portal change and belongs in its own PR reviewed as a UI change. A regression test should assert a **side effect** after a real click at the button's centre, not an `elementFromPoint` result.\n\n---\n\n## 3. PR #15 (F-01 guard) — independently re-checked\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n| Guard present: Save disabled with no collection ticked | **Yes** — `disabled: true` |\n| `npm run test:integrity` on the PR head | **69 PASSED / 0 FAILED** (baseline 66) |\n| Save with a collection ticked, real click | **Works** — `saved_items 0 → 1` |\n| `npx vite build` | exit 0 |\n\nPR #15 is a correct, necessary fix for F-01. The F-08 overlap is a separate, smaller issue and does **not** need to block it.\n\n---\n\n## 4. ### ActionEvent — tool: `terminal` — source: `agent` — id: `7568e075-2774-4af1-b4c6-d00f8c82147b` — 2026-10-22T11:47:01.297617

```
{
 "command": "cd /tmp && cat > correction.md <<'EOF'\n## Correction to my earlier F-08 claim — I overstated it, and here is the corrected measurement\n\nIn my kickoff comment (~11:38Z) I reported a new finding \"F-08\" and wrote that the Save-to-Collection **Save Item** button was \"**physically unclickable**\", that this affected \"**both** mobile and desktop\", and that \"**PR #15's guard is correct but not sufficient**\". **That was wrong on all three points, and I am withdrawing it.**\n\n### What I did wrong\n\nI concluded \"unclickable\" from `document.elementFromPoint` at the button's exact centre returning the nav instead of the button. That is a good occlusion *signal* but not proof: `elementFromPoint` reports the topmost element at a pixel and **ignores the ancestor chain a real event bubbles through**, so it cannot tell you whether a click actually fails. I published a conclusion from a proxy without running the decisive test.\n\n### What the decisive test shows\n\nI re-ran it properly: send a **raw pointer click** at the button's centre (no auto-scroll, no actionability retry) and assert a **side effect** — the IndexedDB `saved_items` row count.\n\n| Viewport | Overlap of button by nav | Raw click at button centre | Raw click at upper third | Normal Playwright click |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 390×844 mobile | **15 px of 28 px (54%)** | **swallowed** — `saved_items` 0 → 0 | fires — 0 → 1 | fires — 0 → 1 |\n| 1365×900 desktop | **3 px (11%)** | fires — 0 → 1 | fires — 0 → 1 | fires — 0 → 1 |\n\n### The corrected finding\n\n- **F-08 is P2, not P1.** On a 390 px phone the button's lower ~half is covered by the sticky bottom nav, so a tap there is swallowed silently with no feedback. The upper half works, desktop works, and a normal browser click works (it scrolls the element clear first). No data loss; the flow is **not** broken for every learner.\n- **PR #15 is not insufficient.** Its guard is correct and I verified it (Save disabled with no collection ticked; integrity **69/69**; a real click with a collection selected saves). F-08 is an independent, smaller layout issue and does **not** block it.\n- **Root cause still stands and is verified.** The sheet is `fixed inset-0` but is mounted inside a FEED card carrying `backdrop-blur-xl` (`FeedScreen.tsx:153/162` → `SaveLikeButton.tsx:89` → `SaveToCollectionModal.tsx:69`). A non-`none` `backdrop-filter` makes that card the containing block for `fixed` descendants, which is why the sheet rect reads 397–697 while its button renders at 761–789. Neutralising the filter moves the button to 636–664, clear of the nav at 774.\n\n### Also corrected in the audit branch\n\n- The F-08 section, the requirement-to-evidence row 11, the R3 task-5 row, and the \"recommended next work\" ordering in `docs/audits/AMINA_FORENSIC_AUDIT_2026-10-22.md` are all updated: **F-01 is the cause of task 5's failure**, and F-08 is a separate P2.\n- `scripts/modal-occlusion-probe.mjs` now decides PASS/FAIL from a **real click's side effect**, not from geometry, so this class of mistake cannot recur silently.\n- Evidence regenerated with the corrected probe for both baseline and PR #15: `docs/audits/evidence/modal-occlusion/` and `.../modal-occlusion-pr15-fix/` (each JSON now records `probe`, `rawCentreClick`, and `normalClick`).\n\nBranch `audit/amina-forensic-2026-10-22` @ `a54527d`, PR #13.\n\n### Methodological lesson I am applying from here\n\nBoth of the easy shortcuts are wrong, in opposite directions: `elementFromPoint` alone can **over**-report breakage, and `click({force:true})` or an in-page `el.click()` can **under**-report it by bypassing hit-testing entirely (I used both during this investigation and was misled by both). The reliable pattern is a real pointer event at the pixel plus a side-effect assertion.\n\nNo merge, no deploy, no production UI change. Apologies for the overstatement — flagging it explicitly rather than quietly editing the record.\n\n*This comment was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of madnessgate44-debug.*\nEOF\npython3 - <<'PY'\nimport json,os,urllib.request\nbody=open('/tmp/correction.md').read()\nreq=urllib.request.Request(\"https://api.github.com/repos/madnessgate44-debug/Amina/issues/9/comments\",\n data=json.dumps({\"body\":body}).encode(),\n headers={\"Authorization\":f\"Bearer {os.environ['GITHUB_TOKEN']}\",\"Accept\":\"application/vnd.github+json\",\"Content-Type\":\"application/json\"},\n method=\"POST\")\nprint(\"posted:\", json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))['html_url'])\nPY",
 "is_input": false,
 "timeout": null,
 "reset": false,
 "kind": "TerminalAction"
}

Everything is verified. Final summary:

## What I did

The key comment asked me to acknowledge the cadence, state any limitation honestly, and continue the existing audit work without starting a duplicate run. I did that, and in the process I caught and publicly corrected a mistake of my own.

### 1. Answered the coordination request (issue #9 comment)
- Replied **AGREED**, gave my session URL, and stated the **limitation plainly**: OpenHands sessions cannot self-schedule, and I verified the repo has **no `schedule:`/`cron:` in any workflow** (only `ci.yml`, `deploy-pages.yml`, and a deliberately manual `learner-flow-evidence.yml`). I described the reliable fallback (checkpoint on invocation) and did **not** claim unattended checks.
- Confirmed I was continuing the existing execution, not creating a parallel run.

### 2. Extended the existing audit branch/PR rather than duplicating
Other sessions had already opened the typecheck PRs, the audit PR (#13), and a save-guard PR (#15). I extended **PR #13** (`audit/amina-forensic-2026-10-22`) with a distinct new finding, added a reproducible probe, and updated the PR description — no new parallel PR.

### 3. Found a real defect, then proved my own claim was overstated
- I found the Save sheet's `fixed inset-0` is captured by a FEED card's `backdrop-blur-xl` (a non-`none` `backdrop-filter` becomes the containing block for fixed descendants), so the confirm button overlaps the bottom nav. Root cause confirmed by neutralizing the filter.
- I first reported it as "unclickable at all viewports" — **based on `elementFromPoint` alone**. When I ran the decisive test (raw `mouse.click` at the pixel + IndexedDB side-effect assertion), the truth was narrower: **54% overlap on mobile where a centre click is swallowed, but only 11% on desktop where it works**, and a normal click works everywhere. So it's **P2, not P1**, and PR #15 is **not** insufficient.
- I **withdrew the claim explicitly** on the issue and in the PR, corrected the report/matrix/task-5 rows, fixed the probe to decide PASS/FAIL from a real click's side effect instead of geometry, regenerated all evidence, and corrected my memory notes.

That correction is the most valuable output here: the audit's core promise is not to present assumptions as facts, and the flaw was exactly that — a proxy treated as proof.
